Where should Wael and Z eat?

A proof of concept: a model trained on Wael's and Z's Beli rankings, reading how Yelp reviewers describe each place. It scores places neither of them has been to, explains why, and combines both tastes into one list. It rests on two people's lists, so the results show that the approach works, not that it is finished.

What moves each person's ranking

Correlation between how a place is described and where it sits on each person's list. Bars right of the line: the more reviewers say this, the higher the place is ranked. Solid bars are unlikely to be chance (p < 0.05).

Six kinds of restaurant

Groups found from review language alone, overlapping (a place can be partly in two). The numbers are each person's average percentile for places in that group, so it shows which kinds each person favours.

The pipeline, stage by stage

Each stage opens to show what goes in, what comes out, the numbers to sanity-check, the decision made there, and what is still open. A stage can be ticked once it has been reviewed (saved in this browser only). The same walkthrough is in PIPELINE.md in the repo.

Does it predict anything?

Each method ranks places it has not seen (5-fold, repeated 5 times). The number is the Spearman correlation between predicted and actual rank. The dashed line is what random guessing reaches 5% of the time; a method has to clear it to count.
